chunks: From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What do you say about sleeping in the mosques?' He said: 'There is no harm, except in the two mosques - the Prophet's Mosque (peace be upon him and his family) and the Sacred Mosque.' He said: 'And he would take my hand during part of the night, move to a side, then sit and converse in the Sacred Mosque, and sometimes he would sleep. I asked him about that, and he said: 'It is only disliked to sleep in the mosque that was during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). As for the one in this location, there is no harm in it.'

key_terms.عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ: time of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sleep in the Prophet's Mosque and the Sacred Mosque according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the general permissibility of sleeping in mosques and the specific dislike (karahah) of doing so in the Prophet’s original mosque in Medina and the Sacred Mosque in Mecca, likely to preserve their sanctity from neglect or impurity. This ruling highlights the unique spiritual status of these two holiest sites in Shia jurisprudence, where maintaining ritual purity and reverence is paramount. The narration further illustrates the Imam’s personal practice of resting in the Sacred Mosque, reinforcing that the restriction is not absolute but context-specific to the historical and sacred significance of the locations.
